_: Feature requests that got a yes, for the roadmap. Edited BY HAND, always.
Nothing automated writes here. Bugs publish themselves; features do not, because
accepting one is a decision and a decision should be a commit with my name on it.
Filing an issue puts it on the tracker. Adding it here puts it on the roadmap.
TWO LEVELS, and the difference is a promise:
accepted   — yes, I am going to build this. Renders as its own entry under
'From your requests', which reads as queued work.
considered — interesting, not committed. Renders into 'Later / maybe', in the
same list and the same tone as everything else parked there.
An issue can be promoted from considered to accepted by moving the entry between
the two arrays; keep the id so the link someone saved still lands.
WHAT NEVER APPEARS HERE, and never appears on the page:
declined   — refused. If the reason is a boundary worth writing down, it earns a
card in 'Considered and set aside' in roadmap.html by hand instead.
duplicate  — folded into whatever it duplicates; add the detail to that entry by
hand if it sharpened it.
enhancement to something already planned — belongs in that § section's prose, by
hand, not as a separate item.
None of those three are automated. A no should cost me a sentence.
Each entry:
id      — anchor, kebab-case, prefixed `req-`. Stable once published.
title   — the heading. Write it as the capability, not as the request.
issue   — issue number it came from, or null.
credit  — GitHub handle to thank, or null. Asked-for, not written-by.
near    — the § section or Later entry it sits beside, or null.
html    — the body, as lines of HTML. Same voice as the rest of the page: first
person, and say what it does not do as well as what it does.
Render with `node scripts/roadmap-data.mjs`.
